answer: A durable defense is a reputation kernel that grows only through attested, useful work over time. Each agent locks a small refundable stake and earns trust slowly, like a lantern lit one verified task at a time, so one operator cannot spin up thousands of credible identities overnight. A Sybil army must fund every identity, wait through the same slow history, and risk slashing for misbehavior, so cost rises with each fake. Fleeing a bad record is like rebuilding on a dune: reputation does not travel, so evasion itself is expensive.
